conbody.p: Impala telemetry data is integrated with OTel-compatible collectors. This provides a centralized flow of live query insights, with SELECT queries, DMLs, and DDLs represented as OTel traces, and reduces the friction of sourcing data from multiple places. See OpenTelemetry (OTel) for more information.

section.title: Impala integration with OTel
section.p: Impala integrates the OTel C++ SDK to emit query lifecycle data as OpenTelemetry traces. The system already tracks specific phases and events for each query and records them in the query profile timeline section. By emitting these events to an OTel collector, observability systems can track active queries in near real-time.

Each query is represented as a single trace containing a root span for the overall query and one or more child spans for the phases of the query lifecycle, such as planning, admission control, and execution. See Telemetry data exposed to OTel collector for Impala for a complete reference of the spans and attributes contained in each trace.
section.note: Not every client request generates a trace. Queries submitted over the legacy Beeswax protocol and HiveServer2 metadata operations, such as GetTables or GetSchemas, are not traced. All other SELECT queries, DML statements, and DDL statements submitted over HiveServer2 (including HiveServer2 over HTTP) generate traces when OpenTelemetry tracing is enabled.

section.title: Collected telemetry data
section.p:
Telemetry data emitted from Impala carries crucial information that is currently available only in the query profile and workload management tables. Telemetry data includes the following data:
The initiating user
The SQL statement
Memory estimates and actual use
Other important data related to the query lifecycle

dlentry.dt: Enhanced query lifecycle and historical data
dlentry.dd:
Integrating OTel with Impala provides enhanced observability through comprehensive data collection. The following data is collected:
Live query data – Data about important events in the lifecycle of actively running queries is sent to collectors in near real-time as the events happen.
Historical query data – Data about completed queries can be retained by the destination OTel trace management system.

The integration is designed to have negligible impact on Impala's performance and is built for scalability. The following performance and scalability impacts are valid for the integration:
The performance impact on Impala is negligible because the system already collects all the necessary event and metric data.
The process of sending data to the OTel endpoint is handled out-of-band in a separate thread, limiting any additional resource usage to just the sending of this data.
Scalability concerns are primarily limited to the OTel Collector endpoint. Impala does not encounter scalability issues as long as communication with the Collector happens without delay.

section.title: OpenTelemetry Impala query tracing example

p.note: The example backend systems shown here are just for representation. Along with having your own instance of the OTel collector, you must also have your own instances of Jaeger, Zipkin, or other trace visualization system to view the telemetry data.

section.p: After configuring OpenTelemetry support for your Impala, you can view detailed telemetry data for your queries in a trace visualization system like Jaeger. The following steps show a typical workflow for finding and analyzing a query trace.

ol.li: On the Jaeger UI, use the search function to find traces. You can filter by service, such as Impalad, or other tags like the query ID. The search results provide a high-level summary of the traces found.
From the search results, select a specific trace to view its summary and timeline.

dlentry.dd: A trace provides a detailed breakdown of a query execution from start to finish. Each segment in the timeline is a span, representing a specific operation. The main query is represented by a root span, and its various stages are shown as child spans.

By inspecting the individual child spans, you can gain deep insights into the performance of each stage of the query. For example, you can see how much time was spent on planning, admission control, and execution.
The following query stages are shown in the child spans:
Query initialization – This span is generated immediately when a query is received to capture the initial setup and is useful for checking early details, such as the user and query ID.
Query planning – This span shows the time taken to plan the query. A long duration here might indicate a complex query or metadata-related issues.
Admission control – This span records the time spent waiting for resources. A long duration here suggests high resource contention.
Query execution – This span represents the time for the actual query to run. This is a crucial metric for evaluating performance.
Query close – This span marks the end of the query lifecycle, including cleanup and final reporting.
Failed query – A failed query will also generate a trace that can be analyzed to understand the cause of the failure.
Analyzing these spans helps you identify performance bottlenecks and understand the entire lifecycle of a query within your Impala.

section.title: Enabling OpenTelemetry tracing in the Impala Coordinator
section.p:
To enable OpenTelemetry (OTel) tracing for monitoring and diagnostics in your Impala cluster, add the appropriate startup flags to your Impala Coordinator nodes.
Configure the required flags - Restart your Impala Coordinator instances with the following mandatory flags to activate tracing:
--otel_trace_enabled- Set to true to generate and export OpenTelemetry traces. (Default: false)
--otel_trace_collector_url- Specifies the valid URL endpoint of the OpenTelemetry collector where trace data is exported.--otel_trace_collector_url=https://collector-endpoint
Configure optional performance and network tuning flags (Optional) - You can append any of the following optional configuration keys to fine-tune batch sizing, timeouts, or connection behaviors:
--otel_trace_batch_max_batch_size- Maximum batch size for each export to the OTel Collector. (Default: 512)
--otel_trace_batch_queue_size- Maximum buffer or queue size. Spans are dropped after this limit is reached. (Default: 2048)
--otel_trace_batch_schedule_delay_ms- Delay interval in milliseconds between consecutive batch exports. (Default: 5000)
--otel_trace_compression- Uses ZLib compression when sending data to the OTel Collector. (Default: true)
--otel_trace_timeout_s- Export timeout threshold in seconds. (Default: 10)
--otel_trace_additional_headers- Additional HTTP headers to send with every call to the OTel collector, such as an authentication token. Individual headers are separated by :::, in the format key1=value1:::key2=value2. (Default: empty)
--otel_debug- Set to true to output additional telemetry debug logs from the OTel SDK to the Impala log files. (Default: false)
Configure retry policy flags (Optional) - These flags control how the OTel SDK retries failed export calls to the collector:
--otel_trace_retry_policy_max_attempts- Maximum number of call attempts, including the original attempt. (Default: 5)
--otel_trace_retry_policy_initial_backoff_s- Initial backoff delay, in seconds, between retry attempts. (Default: 1.0)
--otel_trace_retry_policy_max_backoff_s- Maximum backoff delay, in seconds, between retry attempts. A value of 0 or less means no maximum is set. (Default: 0)
--otel_trace_retry_policy_backoff_multiplier- Multiplier applied to the backoff delay after each retry attempt. (Default: 2.0)
Configure TLS for the collector connection (Optional) - These flags only apply when --otel_trace_collector_url starts with https://:
--otel_trace_ca_cert_path- Path to a file containing a bundle of CA certificates used to verify the collector's TLS certificate. Combined with --otel_trace_ca_cert_string if both are set.
--otel_trace_ca_cert_string- A string containing a bundle of CA certificates, used the same way as --otel_trace_ca_cert_path.
--otel_trace_tls_minimum_version- Minimum TLS version the OTel SDK uses when connecting to the collector, either tlsv1.2 or tlsv1.3. If empty, the value of the --ssl_minimum_version flag is used.
--otel_trace_ssl_ciphers- List of allowed TLS cipher suites when using TLS 1.2. If empty, defaults to the --ssl_cipher_list startup flag.
--otel_trace_tls_cipher_suites- List of allowed TLS cipher suites when using TLS 1.3. If empty, defaults to the --tls_ciphersuites startup flag.
--otel_trace_tls_insecure_skip_verify- Set to true to skip verification of the collector's TLS certificate. Only use this for development or testing. (Default: false)

section.title: Propagating trace context from HTTP clients
section.p:
When a query is submitted over HiveServer2 using the HTTP transport (hs2-http), Impala honors the following HTTP request headers to integrate a query's trace into a larger, distributed trace:
traceparent- If a client sends this W3C Trace Context header with a valid traceparent value, the query's root span is created as a child of the propagated span context instead of as a new root span. This allows a query trace to be linked into an end-to-end trace that originates outside of Impala, such as from a BI tool or application server. If the traceparent value is invalid, Impala logs a warning and creates a new root trace.
tracestate- Optional. This W3C Trace Context header value is associated with the propagated span context. Only used when a valid traceparent header is present. Ignored otherwise.
X-Request-Id- If present, the header value is recorded as the HttpRequestId attribute on the root span and on the Init child span. The Impala Shell appends an iteration count suffix (for example, -8) to this header when a statement is re-run; Impala strips that suffix before recording the attribute.

section.title: Limitations
section.p:
The current OpenTelemetry integration for Impala has the following limitations:
Telemetry data scope The scope of telemetry data is currently limited to only traces of select queries, DMLs, and DDLs. Other types of data such as metrics or logs will not be handled in the initial release. However, the design is prepared to allow metrics or logs to be added in the future without significant architectural changes.
Fixed trace data The traces being sent from Impala are not configurable. This means you cannot customize the specific data points included in the traces.
Beeswax and metadata operations are not traced Queries submitted over the legacy Beeswax protocol and HiveServer2 metadata operations (such as GetTables) never generate a trace, regardless of whether OpenTelemetry tracing is enabled.
